vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule, lab sessions, and grading policy for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn core computer vision concepts ranging from image processing basics and edge detection to deep learning models like CNNs and YOLO. The course grade is composed of 30 percent labs, 30 percent a midterm exam, and 40 percent a final project.
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in linear filtering for image processing.
Edge detection: Techniques like Sobel and Canny used to identify boundaries within images.
Homography: A transformation relating the coordinates of points in different images.
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform used for detecting and describing local features.
RANSAC: An iterative algorithm to estimate mathematical model parameters from noisy data.
Stereo basics: Techniques for depth perception using multiple camera views.
Optical flow: The pattern of apparent motion of objects in a visual scene.
CNN: Convolutional Neural Network used for tasks like image classification.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision - Lecture 01: Introduction
vault.summary: This introductory lecture outlines the course structure, grading policy, and fundamentals of computer vision. It explains how digital images are represented as multidimensional arrays defined by height, width, channels, and uint8 data types. Students are also introduced to essential Python libraries used throughout the course, including numpy, OpenCV, and matplotlib.
key_terms: Height x Width x Channels: The dimensions representing an image as a multi-dimensional array.
dtype uint8: The 8-bit unsigned integer data type commonly used to store pixel intensity values ranging from 0 to 255.
numpy: A foundational Python library for numerical computing and array manipulations.
OpenCV: A widely used open-source computer vision and image processing library.
matplotlib: A plotting library used for visualizing images and data in Python.
